thread:
Aisha (support): Heads-up — customer 'ClearLedger' opened a ticket asking for deterministic JSON streaming for chat+fncall flows. They want 'chunked JSON objects' per event so their ingestion pipeline can process partial outputs.
Luca (product): Can you paste the ticket text? quick summary is fine.
Aisha (support): Sure — key asks: 1) stream valid JSON objects per frame (no partial tokens breaking structure), 2) guarantee fncall metadata (tool name + call args) emitted as its own object, 3) backward-compatible fallback to current streaming format. They flagged latency as critical.
Serena (sales): They commit to Dedicated if we ship that contract. This is a clear revenue trigger. :money_with_wings:
Ravi (eng-ml): Technical note — ensuring syntactically valid JSON per chunk requires us to buffer until a complete object is produced or change generator to emit framed objects. Both have perf tradeoffs.
Maya (eng-runtime): Agree. Two options: a) framing layer that wraps existing token stream with boundaries (adds small latency but minimal model change), b) model-level structured stream (lower client-side reassembly but more invasive).
Luca (product): Requirement candidate: "Streamed JSON objects per event" + example contract. Also need launch criteria: interoperability test suite, benchmark for P99 latency delta <= 50ms for typical chat flows, and fallbacks documented. Thoughts?
Ravi (eng-ml): For (b) we'd need model + tokenizer work; that likely hits Q3. For (a) we can prototype in runtime this sprint. I can mock the framing protocol: each object prefixed with "len:" bytes header or newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON).
Aisha (support): Customer explicitly asked for NDJSON-like semantics — they said newlines are easiest for their pipeline.
Maya (eng-runtime): NDJSON framing is straightforward but fragile if model emits newlines inside fields. Safer is length-prefix or explicit boundary token. We can add an escaping/encode step at runtime.
Luca (product): Prioritization asks: estimate work, risks, and whether this becomes an API contract change. If it's a runtime shim, we might ship as beta behind flag for Hosted and Dedicated.
Ravi (eng-ml): Quick estimates: runtime shim prototype 3 dev-days + 2 days infra tests + 1 day perf runs. Model-level change: 6 wks + evaluation.
Serena (sales): Beta behind flag is fine. Customer wants timeline and ETA to commit. Can we promise a 3-week beta?
Maya (eng-runtime): 3-week delivery to beta is tight but doable if we scope to NDJSON + len-prefixed option and only for chat+fncall stream endpoints. We'll need a canary rollout and auto-fallback to token stream on parse errors.
Luca (product): Acceptance criteria draft: 1) Hosted API supports NDJSON and len-prefixed framing for chat+fncall streaming; 2) Fncall metadata emitted as its own JSON object with standardized keys (tool, args, call_id); 3) Regression: p50/p95 latency within 20/40ms of current baseline for small chats, p99 <= 50ms; 4) Client examples + SDK helpers; 5) Toggle flag + rollout plan.
Aisha (support): I'll update the ticket with these asks and the beta plan.
Ravi (eng-ml): Add test cases: nested JSON in assistant text, mid-call partial objects, and stream interruption handling.
Maya (eng-runtime): Also add telemetry: parse error rate, fallback activations, and latency impact by model/seq len.
Luca (product): Decision: scope minimal runtime shim for Q1 sprint 2, ship beta behind feature-flag to Hosted + Dedicated, and revisit model-level structured streaming as a follow-up initiative. I'll create a product spec PR with the acceptance criteria.
Serena (sales): I'll tell ClearLedger: tentative beta in ~3 weeks, with Dedicated support.
ops-bot: Reminder: create feature flag (product/feat/stream-framing) and set up canary ring after deploy.
Aisha (support): Thanks — updating ticket now and CC'ing customer.
Luca (product): Assign owners: Ravi (eng-ml) + Maya (eng-runtime) for implementation, Luca for spec, Aisha for customer comms. We'll sync briefly in the weekly intake meeting. :white_check_mark:
